<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **95** documentable anchor(s).

**58** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **25** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4783bb98ff854c5b73d3bc127c055b1f15aa64dc` — the merge of head `862f2d1d479fe9ac83382c97de57e79a676d4431` into base `c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4783bb98ff854c5b73d3bc127c055b1f15aa64dc && git checkout 4783bb98ff854c5b73d3bc127c055b1f15aa64dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87 862f2d1d479fe9ac83382c97de57e79a676d4431 && git checkout -B drift-repro c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87 && git merge --no-ff 862f2d1d479fe9ac83382c97de57e79a676d4431

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31961 (S4 #31693) at head a39b4f5a: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

- **Red line 2: the bind never guesses.**
  - `bindStoredPackageReference` re-reads the row and re-asks the one D3 rule at write time. For R3 the caller is the row's own package. For identity columns the caller is none.
  - It writes only when the answer is a refusal and the operator's package is one of the candidates the rule names *now*.
  - A row that resolves, is held by no one, is already bound or is out of scope (R5 managed / R7 open / R8 paused) writes nothing and says why.
  - There is no bind-all. A stale report binds nothing, and a second run writes 0 rows.
- **Red line 1: never looser.** Environment-only rows (D3 (a)) and outside-closure rows (D3 (c)) are reported and refused at bind, with the fix printed (declare the dependency). The bind can never resolve a reference past a package's closure.
- **Red line 3: independently releasable.** No reader, door, URL, MCP or SDK path moves. The report is read-only, and its `--json` is byte-identical across reruns. The bind writes only a column no reader uses yet. The phase-1 one-holder suite is 287/287, and `Metadata-protocol: none` comes with the new ADR-0087 semantic entry. R10 is report-only (its key is the reference). Writer stamping stays with the B children, as ruled.

**Non-blocking.** The write is `update({ id, [column]: package })` with no "still null" condition, so two concurrent binds of one row end as last-write-wins. It's an operator command, so this is low risk. A conditional write (`where column is null`, with 0 rows counted as `already-bound`) would make "a bound row is never moved" hold under concurrency too. The seat decides whether to add it now.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31961 (Fixes #31693, ADR-0150 S4) · 2026-11-09T16:42Z

Head-sha: `0d5bd01b`

- **Form:** draft PR to `main` under `Fixes #31693`. `Clause-②: no`: it adds commands, and existing behaviour is unchanged. `Metadata-protocol: none` (patch). `check-adr-0087-registration` accepts `none` next to the new semantic entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.<id>.ts`, which is the one spec file in the surface (amendment 6743351181).
- **Epic red-line review:** PASS at `a39b4f5a`. After that head:
  - `b317ab39` adds the guarded write the seat ruled. It closes the epic's own non-blocking point, last-write-wins between two concurrent binds.
  - `86bfb04b` is a merge of `main`.
  - `0d5bd01b` rewords one test comment for `check:cross-package-test-inputs`.
  No reader moves, and no red line is touched.
- **`os migrate stored-references`** is read-only. Its `--json` output is byte-identical across reruns. Every row it lists comes from the one D3 rule (`resolvePackageScopedName` / `resolvePackageScopedHolders`; R3 is read from `package_id`), with every candidate, and the D8 tables the composition does not carry are named. There is also a sealed-clash section from `sealBareNameHolders()`. R17 is E6's picklist reader only, and no third traversal is added.
- **`os migrate stored-references bind`** binds one reviewed row.
  - It re-asks D3 at write time, so a stale report binds nothing.
  - The write is guarded on `column $null`. A concurrent bind that lost the race is refused as already bound, naming the stored package.
  - A second run writes 0. There is no bind-all.
  - `environment-only` (D3 a) and `outside-closure` (D3 c) rows are refused, with the fix printed.
  - Each bind leaves one `sys_audit_log` row.
- **Pins and ablations:** integration 8/8, covering ambiguous rows, environment-only R3, the R17 picklist, a sealed clash, a stale report, the race and a CONTROL. Phase-1 one-holder 287/287, rosters 223/223, json-purity 104/104. Four ablations (the three original plus the null guard) each went red, then were restored clean.
- **Deviations accepted:**
  - The confirmation-exit roster now walks topic subcommands.
  - A declined prompt exits 0, as its siblings do.
  - The bind's JSON stdout is pinned in the integration file.
  - Module-top imports for `check:test-source-alias`.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31961` reports NOT governed, +1301/−5. K = 1, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 117/117. CI on this head: 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge:
  - a landing record on #31693, with `pm:dispatched` and `pm:blocking` removed;
  - the epic seat is told, so it can move the B cards whose G parents have closed.
